content:
Hello everyone!
I’m quite new to the Lean community, I’ve been exploring proof assistants for a while as well, and I’d love to get started with the best practices and contribute back to Mathlib4.
What would you recommend me to practice on (specific proofs to write?), before getting started on more advanced topics like Mathlib4?
Best,
Amlal

Hello :wave:
What math are you interested in?
Hey! I don't have a preference on the specific category, I think I should start with what's been heavily formalized first no?
Actually I do have a preference for Abstract Algebra... but I digress
Many things have been formalized, it's hard to recommend stuff without knowing your interests

@Snir Broshi
Would you recommend then practice those formalization first and then explore non-trivial proofs that haven't been formalized later then?
The rationale behind my message is to get familiar as much as possible with Lean's Mathlib4 tactics and those previous formalization to then be able to work through new ones. Let me know what you think.

Could you mention a few stuff in abstract algebra you like?
If it's groups then I'd bet there are many things you could work about showing what the normalizer/centralizer/center of some specific groups is.
e.g. what is Subgroup.normalizer {DihedralGroup.r n}? (I think it's the subgroup of rotations)
If you want to get familiar with Mathlib style tactic usage in a mathematics literate way, fake a look at #mil
@Yakov Pechersky Hello! Thank you so much, I'll have a look at this "mil" channel and I'll do some research on what actions I can take too on it.
It's not a channel, it's a link to community maintained documentation called Mathematics in Lean
@Snir Broshi Let me see if there's some obscure ones I can do first, can I message you if I find anything I think I can formalize?

It's not a channel, it's a link to community maintained documentation called Mathematics in Lean

Oh my bad, thanks for the heads up.
If you find anything you can formalize, then formalize it. Wdym?

Yes I mean that, I'm sorry, English is not my native tongue. French is.
And honestly It's my first time here so I'm kinda nervous too.

Amlal El Mahrouss said:

Yes I mean that, I'm sorry, English is not my native tongue. French is.
And honestly It's my first time here so I'm kinda nervous too.

I wouldn’t be too nervous :sweat_smile: the stakes are not as high as you might be thinking , it’s a community effort most volunteer their time too!

By engaging like this you’ve already earned yourself some good will IMO , because many copy and paste AI, or introduce themselves via an unannounced AI slop PR.
Just for the info I was in similar situation, i started with Theorem proving in Lean4 and it helped alot. Especially the exercises at the end of each section.

I was here one month ago. I didn't quite follow any regular roadmap or suggestion, just simply getting my hands dirty to start. As practice, you might wanna try something from Part III of Serre's book Linear representations of finite groups(if you are interested in).
